CODING_REVIEW_CODEBOOK:
### SCOPE: Explicit scope boundary

Definition: The selected span states a time, component, record, instrument or subject boundary relevant to its proposition.

Include when: A boundary is actually stated and can be transcribed with its source kind.

Exclude when: The reviewer supplies a plausible boundary or treats a requester's proposed scope as an agency's accepted search.

Counterexample: A bare closed label states no searched locations or period.

### ACT: Attributed documentary act

Definition: The span identifies an attributed request, acknowledgment, routing, search statement, determination, grant or judicial act.

Include when: The act and its speaker or instrument can be identified from the unit's located context; keep summary attribution explicit.

Exclude when: A platform stage or reader interpretation is promoted into the underlying instrument or legal effect.

Counterexample: A task named appeal is not proof that an appeal was filed or decided.

### BRIDGE: Explicit evidentiary bridge

Definition: The span actually supplies the linkage needed for the stronger proposition under review.

Include when: The instrument's type, proposition and statutory or procedural scope are explicitly linked; issuance, adjudication and listing eligibility remain distinct.

Exclude when: A co-mention, a cultural association, a matching surname or a plausible custodian is the only connection.

Counterexample: A patent title and grant date do not establish a judicial decision on patent validity.

### QUALIFIER: Qualification of inference

Definition: The unit explicitly limits what its statement, source type or evidence supports.

Include when: A stated qualification limits the proposition; distinguish uncertainty from a definitive negative.

Exclude when: The reviewer adds a caveat that is absent from the unit or treats missing text as an explicit disclaimer.

Counterexample: The absence of a search description is not a statement that no search occurred.

CODING_REVIEW_METHODS:
EntoLaw — prospective located argument review

Unit definition: One declared source span with exact byte digest, parsed-text selector and character offsets; the unit is not a complete request or instrument.

Selection: Purposive contrasts among scope, attribution and evidentiary-linkage problems already identified in this project; not random or exhaustive and not a prevalence denominator.

Codebook version: 2026-11-06-v1

Expected codebook SHA256: 7f204c9f02c470d6db758b796f06ebb613bfb19ec6cd16bdadb34cddf54a0623. Every performed judgment must name this exact digest.

Review plan: Future reviewers would first record source kind and apply each code independently using the include/exclude rules, retaining uncertain decisions and rationales. Discuss disagreements only after preserving original independent judgments; do not backfill them from lexical cues or later consensus. No actual reviewers, independent pairs or judgments are supplied in this edition.

Declared frame: 6 located excerpts; 4 codes. Performed reviewer aliases: 0; explicit judgments: 0; declared independent pairs: 0.

Units are a declared finite excerpt frame, not a probability sample of records, agencies or rhetorical functions. Source kinds remain separate strata; overlapping or repeated passages may be dependent.

A planned review and automatic lexical cues are not human judgments. Missing assignments, explicit uncertainty and explicit absence are distinct states; none is imputed.

Each coefficient uses only the same units and codebook coded present/absent by the named pair. Uncertain or missing decisions are excluded and enumerated. Complete-case selection can distort apparent agreement.

Independence is a reviewer declaration, not an authenticated fact. Consensus/adjudicated labels must not be entered as independent judgments. Multiple coder pairs share units and are never pooled as independent observations.

Observed agreement and Cohen's kappa describe reproducibility of these coding decisions, not truth, rhetorical validity, speaker intent, search adequacy or legal compliance. No universal acceptability threshold, significance test or inferential interval is supplied.

Kappa uses coder-specific marginal proportions: (observed - expected)/(1 - expected). It is withheld for fewer than two complete pairs or expected agreement of one; marginal imbalance can make kappa diverge from raw agreement. Always inspect the contingency cells and coverage.

FIGURE_CAPTION_ARCHITECTURE: How 7 source-owned registries become reproducible outputs. Pure generator methods — metrics, validation, manuscript-variable generation, and figure rendering — turn registry data into inventories, reports, figures, and the rendered manuscript itself. Read as: the package treats the manuscript as a compiled artifact, not as the source of legal facts. Why it matters: readers can audit whether prose, visuals, and counts share the same inputs. Provenance: `src/viz.py`. Caveat: a local build-pipeline description, not a deployment diagram.
FIGURE_CAPTION_CASES_BY_JURISDICTION: The selected case and patent entries by their declared jurisdiction, including court systems and the U.S. patent system. Read as: registry composition; an issued patent and a court judgment are not equivalent legal acts. Why it matters: no frequency of litigation or common rule is inferred from this grouping. Provenance: `src/cases.py`. Caveat: the selected frame supplies neither an exhaustive doctrinal census nor a uniform judicial-holding denominator.
FIGURE_CAPTION_CASES_BY_ROLE: The 18 curated case and patent entries grouped by their registered legal role. This mixed frame includes judicial decisions, an administrative patent appeal and an issued patent. Read as: composition of the selected registry, not litigation rates or doctrinal prevalence. Why it matters: different instrument types require separate legal-effect analysis. Provenance: `src/cases.py` via `src.metrics`. Caveat: an empty role is no evidence that relevant law or records do not exist.
FIGURE_CAPTION_CASE_CANDIDATES_BY_ISSUE: The 176 CourtListener case CANDIDATES the candidate-query pipeline has surfaced so far, grouped by declared legal issue and a conservatively-derived court level (supreme, appellate, trial, other/unknown), with filings by decade in the side panel. Read as: this is a lead list, not a finding -- every bar counts an unreviewed CourtListener opinion-search hit that `status: candidate` in `data/case_candidates.yaml` records and nothing more. Why it matters: it shows where the case law the manuscript has not yet reviewed is concentrated, without letting a search hit stand in for a verified authority. Provenance: `src.case_candidate_metrics` over `data/case_candidates.yaml` and `config/legal_issues.yaml`. Caveat: court level is derived from the court name string alone and is conservative -- a name this rule cannot place stays other/unknown rather than guessed; see `docs/CASE_CANDIDATES.md`.
FIGURE_CAPTION_CITATION_DATES: Date distribution for every bibliography entry with a parseable year, split into broad bands and individual source-date strips with pre-1700 and 1700-1999 layers separated from the 2000+ consolidation, including labelled pre-1800 Rus', Muscovite, and Russian-Imperial legal/scientific sources plus pre-1950 Russian and Soviet entomology/legal sources. Read as: EntoLaw's evidence base is anchored by early legal, regulatory, and treatise sources but interpreted through modern scholarship, cases, statutes, and official materials. Why it matters: the figure makes the historical depth of the citation stack visible instead of leaving it implicit in the reference list. Provenance: `docs/manuscript/references.bib` parsed by `legal_informatics.viz_citation_dates`. Caveat: the date is the bibliography year, so modern editions appear at edition date unless the bibliography declares a source-date anchor. Why it matters: it makes the manuscript's fact-checking boundary auditable by section. Caveat: a section with zero entries may still contain registry-derived facts or qualitative cited claims; this figure shows external/current claims that require a quote-backed verification block.
FIGURE_CAPTION_REGISTRY_FRAME: Read as: jurisdiction by principal registered role for the selected curated decision/patent frame. Why it matters: the joint table exposes the registry composition hidden by separate role and jurisdiction totals. Caveat: authored summaries and year-only dates are not new opinion readings, request durations or a representative sample of legal disputes.
FIGURE_CAPTION_ROLES_OVERVIEW: The 8 registered legal roles an insect can occupy in this release, with the case, statute, species, and milestone evidence encoded for each. Why it matters: the figure sets the manuscript's organizing grammar before the doctrinal sections specialize it. Provenance: `src/roles.py` and `src.metrics.role_coverage_matrix()`. FIGURE_CAPTION_ROLE_INTERCONNECTIONS: Network of the 5 recurring themes that link the legal roles — the definitional problem, the expert-testimony bridge, the biotechnology pivot, the property/conservation mirror, and the ancient/modern rhyme. Edge bundles share a theme colour. Read as: category changes, not species names, are what move a dispute from one legal regime into another. Provenance: `src/interconnections.py`. Why it matters: the synthesis depends on transfers among categories rather than parallel lists of topics. Caveat: the graph encodes declared thematic links, not statistical association.
FIGURE_CAPTION_SPECIES_BY_ROLE: The 24 registered taxa grouped by the legal role they illustrate, from forensic blow flies to quarantined pests, listed species, owned honey bees, engineered and edible insects, the trial weevils, and a weaponized flea. Read as: the same biological class can become evidence, asset, enemy, product, or rights candidate depending on legal context. Why it matters: legal role, not species identity alone, determines which institution acts. Provenance: `src/species.py`. Caveat: an illustrative set chosen to anchor each role, not a taxonomic survey.
FIGURE_CAPTION_STATUTES_BY_CATEGORY: The 43 registered instruments grouped across 9 structural categories — forensic, quarantine, conservation, property, biotech/IP, food, welfare, public-health, and warfare. Read as: regulation follows the legal problem insects pose, not insect taxonomy itself. Why it matters: it shows why the same organism can move between food, biosecurity, conservation, and weapons law. Provenance: `src/statutes.py` via `src.metrics`. Caveat: a representative backbone, not every instrument in each category.
FIGURE_CAPTION_STATUTES_BY_JURISDICTION: The same 43 instruments partitioned by issuing jurisdiction — US-federal, US-state, US-colonial, UK, India, Muscovy, Russian Empire, USSR, EU, and international — showing the field's multi-level legal architecture. Read as: insect law is built through stacked authority, with local movement rules, national statutes, and international instruments all operating at once. Why it matters: no single legal layer owns the field's risk decisions. Provenance: `src/statutes.py`. Caveat: jurisdiction is the issuing level, not a measure of reach or enforcement.
FIGURE_CAPTION_TIMELINE: Selected milestones of entomological law across the 3676-year span the registry encodes, from early bee-theft and bee-property rules to the 2026 monarch-listing suit, coloured by legal role. Read as: old evidentiary and property problems keep reappearing inside new biotechnology, welfare, and conservation disputes. Why it matters: the chronology shows recurrence rather than novelty as the field's basic pattern. Provenance: `src/timeline.py`. Caveat: a selected chronology, not a comprehensive history.

INTERCONNECTION_TABLE:
| Theme | Roles linked | Description |
|---|---|---|
| The definitional problem | Witness / evidence, Regulated threat, Protected subject, Property, Invention / product, Defendant, Moral patient, Weapon | Entomological law is, at root, a series of fights over what category a bug belongs to: is a bumblebee a 'fish', a screwworm a 'plant pest', a fly 'wildlife', an insect 'made by man', a cricket 'sentient'? |
| Expert testimony binds forensic and regulatory law | Witness / evidence, Regulated threat | Proving invasive-pest causation requires the same entomological expertise as proving time of death — a tree-infestation suit failed for lack of an insect expert. |
| Biotechnology is the pivot point | Invention / product, Protected subject, Weapon, Moral patient | GM and gene-drive insects are simultaneously regulated products, conservation tools or threats, potential weapons, and moral patients in farmed-welfare debates. |
| Property and conservation are mirror images | Property, Protected subject | Roman and common-law bee possession rules sit opposite modern bumblebee protection under the same ferae naturae doctrine. |
| The ancient and the cutting-edge rhyme | Defendant, Protected subject, Moral patient | Roman bee pursuit, Irish bee trespass, and the 1587 weevil preserve foreshadow modern fights over habitat, rights, and legally actionable insect status. |
